title: On Shouting across the water for help
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：shout　|　正文 347 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 shout 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the planner ① shouted across the water for help without complaint, and every citizen in the district said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the planner ② shouts across the water for help with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ shout across the water for help at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ shouted across the water for help before — a line in the report for March 1959 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Shouting across the water for help without complaint, the planner said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ shout the news to the whole street with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Shout the news to the whole street at once and never mention it again.

By 1972 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the report, and a new citizen from the next district ⑧ shouts the news to the whole street without complaint every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the square, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ shouted across the water for help again when nobody else would.

⑩ To shout across the water for help, my mother said in 1977, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the district remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the district forgets, somebody shouts across the water for help with great care again and somebody must shout across the water for help without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 喊叫（一般过去式 shouted across the water for help：1965 年规划员头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 喊叫（一般现在 shouts across the water for help：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 喊叫（不定式 to shout across the water for help：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 喊叫（过去完成时 had shouted across the water for help：1959 年三月的规划报告上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 喊叫（动名词 shouting across the water for help 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 大声说（shout the news to the whole street：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去大声说把这消息朝整条街喊出去）
G. v. 大声说（shout the news to the whole street：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 喊叫（后段两处：新来的市民照例 shouts the news to the whole street，而母亲又一次 shouted across the water for help）

answers.why: shout 意为“喊叫”，1965 年规划员毫无怨言地喊叫隔水大声呼救，那是街区里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 shouted。
shout 意为“喊叫”，自那以后规划员小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 shouts。
shout 意为“喊叫”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯喊叫隔水大声呼救”，此处为不定式 to shout across the water for help。
shout 意为“喊叫”，规划报告里 三月 那行字说明早在 1972 年之前就有人喊叫过，故用过去完成时 had shouted。
shout 意为“喊叫”，规划员说“喊叫隔水大声呼救这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 shouting across the water for help 作主语。
shout 意为“大声说”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去大声说把这消息朝整条街喊出去”，should ever 之后用原形 shout the news to the whole street。
shout 意为“大声说”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻大声说把这消息朝整条街喊出去（shout the news to the whole street at once），以后再也不要提起。
shout 意为“喊叫”，新来的市民每个年份都照例大声说把这消息朝整条街喊出去，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 shouts。
shout 意为“喊叫”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地喊叫隔水大声呼救，用一般过去式 shouted 叙述。
shout 意为“喊叫”，结尾那句是母亲 1977 年的话：要喊叫隔水大声呼救，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和街区记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 shout 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1965 the planner shouted across the water for help without complaint, and nobody in the district forgot it.
Even now the planner shouts across the water for help with great care whenever the district asks.
Shouting across the water for help without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever shout the news to the whole street with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new citizen from the next district shouts the news to the whole street without complaint every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother shouted across the water for help again, and the district remembered that half.
